marketed_identity: East Coast Fuzz / Manny's / Orpheum / Clark / related labels
evidence_summary: Specialist historical research identifies at least 11 OEM brandings of the late-1960s East Coast Fuzz family, but the physical manufacturer remains unidentified. Shared regional component sourcing is not treated as proof of Applied, UMI, Universal Amplifier Corp., or any other known builder.

Manny's Fuzz is a prominent marketed state of the East Coast Fuzz family. A surviving 1968 example was reportedly purchased new at Manny's Music on April 19, 1968, establishing a firm public-sales date but not the factory.

Orpheum Fuzz is one of the best documented labels in the East Coast family. A September 1968 St. Louis advertisement provides evidence of commercial distribution; physical-builder attribution remains unresolved.

Clark SS-600 is a core East Coast Fuzz marketed state. It is kept separate from AUL-built Guild Foxey Lady production because similarity of Fuzzrite-derived designs does not establish a common factory.
Mica-Tone is identified among the East Coast Fuzz OEM labels by specialist research. It remains below public-promotion threshold because the surviving factory trail is incomplete.
Gracin's is identified as a New York East Coast Fuzz marketed state. No direct physical-builder document has been located.

AUL is independently documented as the New York manufacturer contracted by Guild for the second Foxey Lady production after the Mosrite run. This known AUL relationship must not be used to assign AUL to the unrelated East Coast Fuzz family.
Guild's grey Foxey Lady transitional run is attributed to AUL Instruments in New York. It is a separate OEM branch from the unknown-builder East Coast Fuzz family.
